title: spaCR screens
description: Follow a pooled image-based screen from Home through image measurements, phenotype classification, barcode counts and regression.
introduction: Start on Home with the data you have. For a pooled image-based screen, use Mask and Measure to prepare image measurements, then Annotate and Classify to obtain phenotype scores. Use Map Barcodes for sequencing reads. Bring the scores and guide counts together in Regression, matching plate and well identifiers. Begin at the step that matches your existing results.
conclusion: Before opening Regression, match the plate and well identifiers in your scores, guide counts and experimental layout. Keep the annotation column, classifier settings and barcode references with the run. Follow the linked module lessons for each step, or choose the pooled-screen walkthrough on Home for guided navigation.

mask.name: Mask
mask.guidance: Select channels and models, inspect a preview, then run Mask. Measure consumes the merged arrays; the counts database is not yet a feature table.

consumes.description: raw files in src, orig/ or consolidated/

produces.description: image channels and label masks, one array per field
object counts and the run-status stamp
per-object label arrays; removed by cleanup

declared_ports.summary: raw microscope files to merged arrays carrying label masks

measure.name: Measure
measure.guidance: Measure reads images and label planes together. Enable crop saving if you need PNG files; keep the database and source project together for streamed crops.

consumes.description: one array per field, written by mask

produces.description: single-object PNGs, when save_png is on

declared_ports.summary: merged arrays to per-object measurements and crops

annotate.name: Annotate
annotate.guidance: Label representative objects in png_list before supervised training. Use separate annotations for different questions and keep training and evaluation groups independent.

classify_merged.name: Classify
classify_merged.guidance: Choose Computer Vision for crops or streamed object images, or Tabular Machine Learning for measured feature columns. The two families consume different inputs.

consumes.description: the feature table, and png_list when the image classifier is the one being fitted
the crops themselves, when not read from a tar

produces.description: per-object scores merged back into the database

declared_ports.summary: crops or measured features to a trained classifier and per-object scores

map_barcodes.name: Map Barcodes
map_barcodes.guidance: Supply the references that encode your experiment. Inspect mapped counts and barcode QC before pairing well-level guide counts with phenotype scores.

produces.description: one row per read, with its three barcodes

declared_ports.summary: FASTQ reads to row / column / gRNA barcode assignments

regression.name: Regression
regression.guidance: Match plate and well identifiers across phenotype and guide-count inputs, select the response and controls, and inspect diagnostics before interpreting hits. Direct measured responses are also supported.

declared_ports.summary: measurements plus a barcode map to gene-level hits

pooled_screen.title: A pooled spaCR screen

steps.action: Start on Home and open Mask. Load the example data, check channels and segmentation, then run.
Return Home and open Map Barcodes for the matching sequencing reads and references.

If segmentation already exists, import the matching images and external masks into a spaCR project and inspect the resulting object identities. Skip segmentation and proceed to Measure when its required arrays are present.
Open Measure with the Mask project and create measurements and object crops.
Open Annotate, inspect representative objects and save phenotype labels.

Define threshold or polygon gates on actual feature/coordinate columns, then apply the saved gate to compatible objects. Use Annotate to write the displayed gates to an annotation column; review the selected objects and choose binary or multiclass labels.

Project measured features or supplied encoder features and inspect representative crops. A cluster is a candidate grouping, not a validated phenotype. Use the lasso and annotation controls to write reviewed selections to an annotation column in the matching measurement database. A geometric selection alone does not establish a biological phenotype.
Open Classify, choose images or measured features, and inspect held-out predictions.
Open Regression with compatible phenotype scores and per-well guide counts; inspect hits and diagnostics.

pooled_screen.description: Combine image-derived phenotypes with guide abundance to rank perturbations. Segment and measure images, create reviewed labels with Annotate, Gate Editor or Image UMAP, and train and validate a classifier. Map the matching sequencing reads on an independent branch. Join compatible phenotype scores and guide counts by experimental identity for Regression. Annotation and segmentation routes are alternatives, not requirements to run every branch.

inputs.title: Microscopy images
inputs.description: Supply the original microscopy images with channel identities and field naming. For a time series, preserve frame order and timing. Choose segmentation settings appropriate for the objects in this experiment.

inputs.title: Existing masks and matching images
inputs.description: Import source images together with matching integer object-label masks. Preserve object classes and field identities. This is an alternative to generating new masks; inspect the imported project before measuring.

inputs.title: FASTQ: R1/R2, R1 only or R2 only
inputs.description: Supply gzipped FASTQ files and the barcode reference CSVs. Use paired mode for R1/R2. For single-end reads, choose single mode and set single_direction to R1 or R2 to match the files and extraction orientation.

connections.handoff: Use the same project and the correct image/mask channel indices.
Save or stream crops with stable object identities.
Choose the image or tabular family to match your input.
Keep labelled training and evaluation groups separate.
Select the intended CV or ML score column and preserve plate/well identity.
Pair guide counts with phenotype scores using consistent plate/well keys.
